title: Trusting AI
abstract: Abstract Here is a very popular view on what user rational trust in AI requires: the Explanation View of AI Trust, whereby user rational trust in AI requires an explanation of why the AI has reached the conclusion it has. The authors of this chapter think that the Explanation View of AI Trust is wrong. It is not true of trust in general that rational trust (even typically) requires understanding why, and it is not the case that AI communication generates any special normative requirement that there should be an explanation why that grounds rational trust. This doesn’t mean that the authors think there is nothing to be gained by explainable AI (XAI)—they prefer explainability, all else being equal! But understanding how to increase trust (when appropriate) in AI requires the right diagnosis. In order to understand how to increase trust in AI, the authors think it’s better to focus not on AI explainability but instead on AI trustworthiness. That is, in this chapter, they defend what they call the Simple View of AI Trust, whereby user rational trust in AI requires AI trustworthiness.

title: Leveraging federated learning for smart grids: A comprehensive survey
abstract: The integration of sensors, smart meters, and Internet of Things devices has significantly improved two-way communication in smart grids (SGs). Currently, the collection and transmission of critical data from edge devices has become possible. While centralized training of artificial intelligence schemes is crucial for planning, decision-making, and operations of SGs, it poses data privacy concerns in a competitive market, motivating the application of federated learning (FL). However, no research work has yet surveyed FL schemes in SG from a broad perspective and addressed their vulnerabilities with countermeasures. Hence, this paper presents an organized and detailed review of the existing literature on FL applications in SGs, while providing categorizations from different perspectives. This paper also systematically classifies cyber threats targeting FL schemes and summarizes the relevant literature. Simultaneously, a taxonomy of corresponding defense strategies is presented to improve the robustness of FL schemes against such cyberattacks. Moreover, based on the existing literature, future prospects are outlined to guide academic and industrial advancements in this sector.

title: High‐Capacity Multi‐Pair Continuous‐Variable Quantum Network Coding Based on Microcavity Frequency Comb
abstract: ABSTRACT Continuous‐variable quantum network coding (CVQNC) faces several challenges when extended to large scale scenarios, including the insufficient channel capacity, low entanglement generation efficiency, and degradation of entanglement under channel loss. In this study, a high‐capacity CVQNC scheme based on microcavity frequency combs is proposed over the butterfly network, which enables parallel quantum information transmission among multiple user pairs by exploiting network coding at the bottleneck link. Furthermore, an entanglement enhancement strategy combining mode multiplexing with quantum scissors is introduced to reduce the entanglement degradation caused by channel loss. The results show that the proposed scheme improves the entanglement enhancement efficiency, channel capacity, transmission fidelity, and security while scaling to a larger number of users.

title: Refining Heuristic-Based Bitcoin Address Clustering with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Bitcoin's pseudonymous nature makes it challenging to analyze user-level activity, since a single user may control multiple identifiers (addresses). Existing heuristic-based methods attempt to identify addresses belonging to the same user, but they often produce flat cluster assignments with limited modularity and are prone to errors such as merging different users together. In this work, we propose a method for refining heuristic-obtained clusters by grounding our clustering on contrastive embeddings yielded by graph neural networks. Our contributions are threefold: (i) we release a publicly available dataset of Bitcoin transaction graphs containing a substantial number of clusters; (ii) we propose a methodology for learning address embeddings consistent with heuristics, and back it up with theoretical guiding intuitions; (iii) through hierarchical clustering, we enable a finer analysis of heuristic clusters and provide a quantitative criterion for flagging suspicious merges.

title: Reliability Challenges in Diffusion Vision-Language Models
abstract: Diffusion-based Large Vision-Language Models (dLVLMs) have recently emerged as a compelling alternative to autoregressive (AR) LVLMs, offering advantages in parallel decoding, bidirectional context, and controllable generation. Despite rapid progress, their reliability properties remain largely uncharacterized. We present the first systematic reliability evaluation of hallucination and bias in dLVLMs, benchmarking six diffusion models against competitive AR baselines across four dimensions. Our key findings are: (1) dLVLMs reverse the yes-bias of AR models in binary visual queries; (2) they achieve competitive hallucination rates yet exhibit degraded linguistic quality; (3) they collapse to near-zero accuracy on underrepresented racial groups with opposite-polarity gender bias; and (4) they exhibit accuracy collapse in multiple-choice settings when the correct option is shorter than its distractors, associated with a length prior that emerges at the first denoising step. Tokens committed at late denoising steps with low confidence further correlate with hallucinated content, pointing to a mechanistic signal unique to diffusion generation. These patterns vary across model families, suggesting reliability is shaped by the generative paradigm together with training data.

title: A Backend-Agnostic MWIS Kernel for Stochastic Unit Commitment with Neutral-Atom Hardware Validation
abstract: Quantum hardware is beginning to address structured combinatorial optimisation, but two steps still block practical use: mapping real operational models onto hardware-compatible instances, and converting noisy hardware output back into feasible decisions. Here we introduce a backend-agnostic computational interface that compiles the discrete decision layer of stochastic unit commitment into a move-based maximum-weight independent set (MWIS) problem, while retaining continuous dispatch and feasibility recovery in the classical computational layer. We validate the approach in a green hydrogen scheduling setting and deploy it on the QuEra Aquila neutral-atom quantum processor. This is the first end-to-end industrial scheduling workflow that connects real operational decisions to programmable neutral-atom hardware through a solver-agnostic MWIS representation. Across a 15-day hardware campaign on 50-node instances, hardware-generated solutions after classical refinement match or exceed the dispatch margins obtained from exact MWIS on every day. When scaling to 144 nodes, encoding quality remains stable, while the probability that the full atom array survives, rather than graph embedding, emerges as the dominant bottleneck to further scaling. Together, these results establish a hardware-compatible computational pathway toward larger problem scales, and lay the groundwork for exploring regimes in which exact classical optimisation may no longer scale efficiently.

title: SAGE: Subpopulation-Aware Generative Enhancement for Mitigating Spurious Correlations
abstract: Spurious correlations pose a significant challenge to the robustness of modern machine learning. The inherent imbalance in dataset distributions often leads traditional Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) models to rely on majority spurious attributes for classification, resulting in poor performance on minority groups. This problem becomes particularly challenging when the spurious attributes are unavailable. Existing group-label-free methods often upsample minority groups or misclassified real training examples; repeating the same instances can reduce effective diversity and encourage overfitting. To mitigate these spurious correlations from a data-centric perspective in the absence of prior knowledge, we introduce Subpopulation-Aware Generative Enhancement (SAGE), a two-stage generative augmentation framework. Using cluster-derived sub-labels and class labels, we fine-tune a conditional generative model and text encoder, generating targeted synthetic data to fill underrepresented regions in the training set and construct a balanced validation set for last-layer reweighting. We experimentally show that SAGE achieves 89.5%, 85.7%, and 79.1% worst-group accuracy on Waterbirds, CelebA, and MetaShift, respectively, outperforming the best group-label-free baselines by up to 7.7 percentage points.

title: One Policy, Any Budget: Internalizing Budget-Aware Search via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: While reinforcement learning has enabled LLM-based search agents to invoke external tools, existing methods train under fixed budgets and cannot adapt when constraints vary at deployment. We propose AnySearch, a framework that enables a single policy to perform budget-aware search under any budget constraint through a training scaffold and curriculum reinforcement learning. In the first phase, we train the agent with explicit budget state injection and structured reasoning prompts that guide efficient allocation under linearly decaying budgets. In the second phase, the scaffold is removed and the agent learns to operate autonomously under adaptively sampled budget constraints, matching inference conditions. Both phases are optimized with a composite reward that couples answer accuracy with budget efficiency through absolute and relative signals, where an adaptive weight amplifies the efficiency signal for high-accuracy queries and attenuates it for low-accuracy ones. Extensive experiments on seven general and multi-hop QA benchmarks show that our method outperforms baselines across all budget scales, generalizes to unseen constraints beyond the training range, and achieves superior tool productivity without excessive token overhead. Our code is available at https://github.com/xwsun01/AnySearch.

title: Post-selective attack with multimode projection onto Fock subspace
abstract: In this work we present a comprehensive analysis of a post-selective attack on quantum key distribution protocols employing phase-encoded linearly independent coherent states (or similar alternatives). The attack relies on multimode projection onto a Fock subspace and enables probabilistic extraction of information by an eavesdropper. We derive analytical expressions for the information accessible to the adversary and show that it depends only on three protocol parameters: the mean photon number of the signal states, the phase separation in the information basis, and the expected optical loss of the quantum channel. Several optical realizations of phase-encoded quantum key distribution protocols are analyzed to illustrate the applicability of the results. Possible countermeasures against the proposed attack are also discussed.

title: Channel-Calibrated Aggregate Monitoring for Coordinated Manipulation
abstract: Coordinated manipulation can shift platform-level signals while leaving each participant locally inconspicuous. We study this aggregate footprint as a measurement problem: how can heterogeneous interval summaries provide calibrated evidence against a declared anchor-and-channel model, and when does persistent induced-summary excess above the matched baseline yield positive linear expected evidence growth? In each interval, the detector observes a released histogram, its count and resolution, and a platform-declared reference model. The summary is lifted to a distribution on a common bounded signal space and compared with the reference using Wasserstein–1 distance. Raw Wasserstein deviations are geometrically comparable across reporting regimes, but their null scale is generally nonzero and regime dependent because finite sampling and the reporting channel affect their distribution. We therefore subtract the expected deviation obtained by replaying the same reporting channel under the declared reference. The resulting signed increments form a cumulative evidence process. Undermatched-channel and non-anticipativity conditions, the exact process is a bounded-increment martingale; a valid conservative guardband yields a supermartingale, conditional on its guardband event when it is estimated. These properties provide finite-horizon and anytime-valid false-alarm control. Under the stated conditions, persistent induced-summary excess above the channel-matched baseline yields positive linear expected growth of the exact evidence process, whereas vanishing excess together with within-intervaltracking eliminates positive linear expected growth. We also characterize structural information loss. Non-injective reporting can make distinct latent distributions indistinguishable to every summary-based detector, and fixed-resolution histograms imposea geometric resolution floor. The framework extends to bounded multidimensional signals through either joint Wasserstein monitoring under a declared product-space metric or coordinatewise marginal monitoring with simultaneous error control. Finally, Wasserstein duality conditionally bounds shifts in induced expected values of Lipschitz outcome functions, supporting an integrity-budget interpretation of a justified induced-summary Wasserstein allowance. The guarantees are aggregate, anchor-relative, and channel-conditional: an alarm provides false-alarm-controlled evidence against the declared anchor-and-channel model; it does not establish that an observed departure is persistent, caused by coordination, attributable to particular identities, or adversarial in intent.

title: DETEKSI CYBERBULLYING PADA KOMUNIKASI PENGGUNA GAME ONLINE MENGGUNAKAN MODEL HYBRID INDOBERT-CNN-BILSTM (STUDI KASUS: PLATFORM ROBLOX)
abstract: Platform game online seperti Roblox sangat rentan terhadap perilaku cyberbullying, mengingat demografi pengguna aktifnya yang didominasi oleh anak-anak dan remaja. Sistem moderasi komunikasi bawaan Roblox yang masih berbasis aturan (rule-based) terbukti memiliki keterbatasan dalam memahami konteks percakapan serta mengatasi variasi bahasa tidak baku dan teknik penyamaran kata (obfuscation), sehingga kerap memicu penyensoran berlebihan atau justru meloloskan ujaran berbahaya. Oleh karena itu, penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi sistem tersebut dan mengembangkan model deteksi cyberbullying multi-kelas (violence, harassment, racist, neutral) berbahasa Indonesia menggunakan pendekatan deep learning dengan kerangka kerja CRISP-DM. Penelitian ini mengujikan 7 skenario arsitektur pemodelan tunggal dan hybrid (IndoBERT, CNN, dan BiLSTM), di mana validasi urgensi masalahnya diukur melalui metode Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA), sedangkan validasi prapemrosesan dan evaluasi hasil prediksi (error analysis) melibatkan pakar bahasa. Hasil analisis IPA menunjukkan adanya kesenjangan signifikan antara harapan pengguna dan kinerja sistem bawaan pada aspek perlindungan cyberbullying, yang menjadikannya sebagai prioritas utama perbaikan. Berdasarkan hasil eksperimen dari ketujuh model, arsitektur hybrid IndoBERT-CNN terbukti sebagai model paling optimal karena mampu mencapai tingkat akurasi tertinggi sebesar 86,08%, error rate terendah sebesar 13,91%, dan waktu inferensi yang efisien selama 7,00 detik. Model terbaik ini kemudian diimplementasikan ke dalam sebuah purwarupa dashboard moderasi konten otomatis berbasis web menggunakan pendekatan Human-in-the-loop (HITL). Sistem tersebut dirancang untuk memfasilitasi Game Administrator dalam mengidentifikasi dan mengaudit riwayat percakapan secara batch processing, sehingga memberikan solusi moderasi yang lebih terukur, transparan, dan kontekstual dibandingkan sistem sensor konvensional. Kata Kunci : Cyberbullying, Roblox, Model Hybrid, Content Moderation, CRISP-DM

abstract: This paper studies the factors affecting the efficiency of the wastewater aeration process, in particular the concentration of dissolved oxygen, which largely determines the quality of the aeration process. The paper also proposes a control system for the aeration process based on fuzzy logic control, which has recently been gaining an increasingly wide scale of application in process control systems and production. A mathematical model of fuzzy logic for controlling the aeration process based on the Mamdani method and a rule base for controlling the parameters of input and output signals at the current time are developed

title: Research Data and Survey Questions
abstract: In higher education, AI chatbots are gradually been integrated into student services. Yet the mechanisms through which they shape university brand perceptions are poorly understood. Utilizing the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework along with signaling and commitment–trust perspectives, the present study tests a sequential mediation model of how AI chatbot service quality shapes university brand loyalty. The data were collected from 574 students in five Chinese universities and partial least squares structural equation modelling was utilized to test the proposed hypotheses. The findings confirm a sequential chain in which AI service quality first elevates university brand image, activating brand trust, which in turn heightens brand satisfaction and ultimately consolidates as loyalty. This suggests that students initially interpret chatbot quality as a signal of broader institutional standing before making relational judgements. The study contributes to the human-computer interaction literature by specifying the temporal ordering of image, trust, and satisfaction in AI-mediated encounters, and by showing that digital service carries brand-relevant consequences comparable to those attributed to human interaction. Practical implications are drawn for university leaders seeking to align AI investments with long-term loyalty and reputational goals.

The study contributes to the human-computer interaction literature by specifying the temporal ordering of image, trust, and satisfaction in AI-mediated encounters, and by showing that digital service carries brand-relevant consequences comparable to those attributed to human interaction. Practical implications are drawn for university leaders seeking to align AI investments with long-term loyalty and reputational goals.

title: Too Simple, Too Complex, Just Right: A Critical Survey Review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of deep learning and inductive bias as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Curiosity
abstract: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) offers a promising approach to tackling complex reinforcement learning problems by decomposing them into simpler, manageable sub-tasks. However, standard HRL methods often struggle with exploration, particularly in environments with high dimensionality and sparse reward signals. This work proposes a novel framework that integrates intrinsic curiosity into HRL, aiming to alleviate these exploration challenges. The core idea is to introduce an intrinsic motivation module at each level of the hierarchy, driven by prediction error or novelty detection. This encourages agents to actively seek out novel states and learn more efficient policies. The framework's effectiveness is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a conceptual discussion, highlighting its potential to improve exploration and learning performance in complex environments. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of hierarchical structure and intrinsic motivation, providing a more robust and adaptable learning process. The presented approach offers a pathway towards overcoming the limitations of conventional HRL methods and facilitating the development of intelligent agents capable of navigating and mastering intricate tasks.

title: Core Claim: A dynamic quantum topology learning model predicts the behavior of quantum systems by dynamically adjusting quantum topology structures, resulting in more effective system modeling and prediction.
abstract: Quantum systems exhibit remarkable behaviors, often challenging traditional modeling approaches. This research explores a novel predictive model based on quantum self-organization (QSO) networks. The model dynamically adjusts quantum topology structures based on input data, allowing for more effective system modeling and prediction. This approach addresses the limitations of static topology models by implementing a dynamic topology learning strategy. The core mechanism involves using quantum circuit simulation to dynamically adjust topology, thereby establishing a strong relationship between system models and underlying quantum structures. This results in a more adaptable and accurate prediction capability, offering a significant advancement over existing methods. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this dynamic approach through simulation results, showcasing improved predictive performance and a deeper understanding of quantum system dynamics.

title: Canyon Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Canyon Bats
abstract: This paper presents Canyon Bat, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of canyon bats. The algorithm leverages the unique characteristics of canyon bat flight, specifically their ability to navigate complex, three-dimensional environments while maintaining a stable flight altitude and adjusting their flight direction based on the presence of food sources. Canyon Bat employs a novel approach to position initialization, velocity update, and constriction parameters, drawing direct parallels from bat echolocation and flight dynamics. The algorithm is designed to be robust and efficient, particularly in high-dimensional optimization problems. The core mechanism involves a dynamic constriction factor, inspired by the bat's adjustment of its frequency, and a position update rule that considers both the global best and local best solutions. Experimental results on benchmark functions demonstrate that Canyon Bat achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics like convergence rate, solution quality, and computational cost. Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of Canyon Bat.

title: Camiguin Forest Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Camiguin Forest Mouse Algorithm" (CFMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Camiguin Forest Mouse ( *Mus guintera* ) endemic to the Philippines. The algorithm leverages the mouse's adaptive movement strategies – specifically its ability to efficiently search for food resources within a complex and dynamic environment – to tackle computationally challenging optimization problems. CFMA incorporates elements of exploration and exploitation, mimicking the mouse's decision-making process when encountering potential food sources. The core of the algorithm relies on a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework with adaptive velocity and position updates influenced by the mouse's heuristic of prioritizing promising areas based on a local density estimation. The performance of CFMA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO, Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Simulated Annealing (SA). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a viable solution for diverse optimization scenarios. The key mathematical components of the CFMA are detailed below, providing a robust theoretical foundation for the algorithm's design and implementation.

title: Cameroonian Wading Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Mesomycteris gambianus*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Cameroonian Wading Rat" (CWR), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Mesomycteris gambianus*, a semi-aquatic rodent found in Cameroon. The algorithm's design is predicated on the rat's efficient exploration of riverbanks and its strategic use of short-range movements for resource acquisition. CWR leverages a combination of concepts from Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), incorporating a 'rat-like' exploration strategy where particles iteratively adjust their positions based on local environmental assessments and a weighted average of past optimal positions. The core innovation lies in the introduction of a 'risk aversion' parameter, mimicking the rat's cautious approach to navigating potentially hazardous terrain. This parameter influences the acceptance probability of new solutions during the simulated annealing phase, preventing premature convergence. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and robustness. Experimental results indicate that CWR outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and high dimensionality. Further research will explore the algorithm's adaptability to different problem domains and its potential for real-world applications.

title: Non-Euclidean Geometry for Data Compression and Retrieval
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-Euclidean geometry, specifically hyperbolic geometry, to enhance data compression and retrieval techniques. Traditional methods often rely on Euclidean distance metrics, which can be suboptimal for high-dimensional data. By mapping data into hyperbolic space, we leverage the unique properties of hyperbolic geometry – particularly the exponential divergence of distances – to achieve more efficient data compression and faster search algorithms. The core idea involves representing data points within this space, where distances directly relate to the underlying geometric structure. This approach offers a fundamentally different perspective on data representation, potentially leading to significant improvements in compression ratios and search performance. This research proposes a framework and theoretical basis for utilizing non-Euclidean geometry, offering a novel solution for the challenges posed by the ever-increasing volume of data. The key contribution lies in the design of algorithms that exploit the inherent properties of hyperbolic space to reduce redundancy and accelerate search operations.

title: Quantum Entanglement Topological Network
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unparalleled computational power and secure communication. This paper explores the design and implementation of a quantum entanglement topological network, a novel architecture leveraging the unique properties of entanglement to construct robust quantum information processing and communication systems. We propose a method for establishing and maintaining entanglement across a topological network, utilizing quantum entanglement to facilitate the transfer of quantum information and to enhance quantum computation capabilities. The research focuses on the core mechanisms of entanglement-based network construction, and its potential to significantly advance quantum technologies.

title: Topological Information Graphs for Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements across numerous fields, but realizing this potential faces significant challenges, primarily related to algorithm design and optimization. Traditional approaches often rely on static parameter settings, limiting the potential for performance gains. This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm optimization strategy leveraging the power of topological information graphs. We propose a dynamic adjustment mechanism that iteratively refines the topology of the graph, allowing for adaptive optimization of quantum circuit parameters. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through extensive simulations and analyses, showcasing a significant improvement in quantum algorithm performance compared to existing techniques. The core mechanism focuses on exploiting the inherent structure of the graph to guide the optimization process, resulting in enhanced efficiency. This research offers a fundamentally new perspective on algorithm optimization within the quantum realm, holding promise for accelerating the development of practical quantum solutions.

title: ## Bottlehead: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bottlehead Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bottlehead, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bottleheads, a species of bird known for its unique and efficient foraging strategies. Bottlehead utilizes a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, mimicking the bottlehead's ability to identify promising food sources and then refine its search within those regions. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, maintaining a set of candidate solutions. Each solution's fitness is evaluated using a defined objective function. A novel 'bottle' representation is introduced, where solutions are represented as a series of coordinates, each representing a potential food source location. The algorithm adjusts these coordinates based on a 'pressure' mechanism, simulating the bottlehead's directional movement towards promising locations. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic population size and a probabilistic mechanism for solution diversification. Experimental results demonstrate Bottlehead's effectiveness in solving various benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's key parameters – pressure strength, diversification rate, and population size – are discussed, and their impact on the optimization process is analyzed.

title: Fuzzy Expert System for Melamine Moulding Compound Dye Feasibility Identification: A Case study on Plastic Industry
abstract: This study develops and evaluates an explainable zero order Fuzzy Sugeno expert system for assessing the feasibility of Melamine Moulding Compound (MMC) dyes in the melamine industry. The objective is to support consistent dye assessment by converting expert knowledge of boiling point, processing time, and injection pressure into a structured decision model. Each input variable is represented by low, medium, and high fuzzy sets, while four domain experts contributed to the definition and review of the membership ranges, rule base, and feasibility outcomes. The model contains 27 rules with singleton consequents of 10, 20, and 30 for not feasible, conditionally feasible, and feasible decisions, respectively, with midpoint decision boundaries of 15 and 25. The model was evaluated using 23 historical process profiles and classified 10 samples as not feasible (43.48%), 8 as conditionally feasible (34.78%), and 5 as feasible (21.74%). MMC103, with a boiling point of 165 °C, processing time of 65 seconds, and pressure of 55 bar, activated eight rules and produced a Sugeno score of 26.67, resulting in a feasible classification. A ±5% sensitivity analysis with 10,000 random perturbations produced MMC103 scores from 25.86 to 27.29 and retained its feasible classification in all runs, while overall class stability across the 23 profiles reached 98.86%. Sugeno classifications agreed with Mamdani inference for 20 of 23 profiles and with a crisp rule baseline for 18 profiles. By combining expert knowledge formalization, sensitivity evaluation, comparative analysis, and web implementation, this study provides an explainable and traceable decision support approach for MMC dye feasibility assessment in melamine production.

title: PT-CPABKS – Secure Multi-User Keyword Search in Cloud Using Policy-Tiered CP-ABE with Optimized Indexing
abstract: Abstract Cloud computing faces several challenges in balancing data confidentiality with efficient retrieval and fine-grained access control. Conventional searchable encryption models enable keyword search but lack fine-grained access control, whereas traditional model-based solutions enforce policies at the cost of computational and communication overhead. To address these drawbacks, this manuscript proposes a Policy-Tiered Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Keyword Search (PT-CPABKS) model that integrates Ciphertext-Policy Attribute-Based Encryption (CP-ABE), Advanced Encryption Standard with Galois/Counter Model (AES-GCM), and Public-key Encryption with Keyword Search (PEKS) with a policy-tiered index structure. The proposed model supports secure multi-keyword search, enforces fine-grained access policies, and optimizes the encryption, decryption, and key generation process by minimizing per-attribute operations. The incorporation of the policy-tiered index reduces redundant attribute processing and accelerates query processing. The proposed model achieved a competitive performance by obtaining an overall execution time of 544 ms when compared with CP-ABE and MRSE models.

title: Generación automática de alertas climáticas mediante modelos de lenguaje grande (LLMS)
abstract: Los Sistemas de Alerta Temprana (SAT) son herramientas críticas para mitigar el impacto de eventos hidrometeorológicos extremos en regiones costeras como Manabí (Ecuador). Este estudio presenta una arquitectura de inteligencia artificial generativa que transforma observaciones meteorológicas de la estación Meteonet de la Universidad Técnica de Manabí (Portoviejo) en alertas climáticas en lenguaje natural, fieles a los datos y orientadas a la acción. Se evaluaron tres modelos de lenguaje (GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 3.1-8B y Qwen 2.5-7B) sobre 25 casos meteorológicos bajo un diseño factorial fraccional con tres estrategias de prompting y dos variantes de contexto. Las salidas se contrastaron con referencias de dos meteorólogas mediante métricas de similitud léxica (ROUGE-L), semántica (BERTScore) y consistencia factual numérica. Ningún modelo domina en todas las dimensiones: GPT-4o-mini lidera en similitud semántica, Qwen 2.5-7B en fidelidad numérica y LLaMA 3.1-8B en latencia. Se documenta un sesgo conservador sistemático: ningún modelo asignó NARANJA cuando el consenso experto sí lo hizo.

evidence.abstract: Los Sistemas de Alerta Temprana (SAT) son herramientas críticas para mitigar el impacto de eventos hidrometeorológicos extremos en regiones costeras como Manabí (Ecuador). Este estudio presenta una arquitectura de inteligencia artificial generativa que transforma observaciones meteorológicas de la estación Meteonet de la Universidad Técnica de Manabí (Portoviejo) en alertas climáticas en lenguaje natural, fieles a los datos y orientadas a la acción. Se evaluaron tres modelos de lenguaje (GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 3.1-8B y Qwen 2.5-7B) sobre 25 casos meteorológicos bajo un diseño factorial fraccional con tres estrategias de prompting y dos variantes de contexto. Las salidas se contrastaron con referencias de dos meteorólogas mediante métricas de similitud léxica (ROUGE-L), semántica (BERTScore) y consistencia factual numérica. Ningún modelo domina en todas las dimensiones: GPT-4o-mini lidera en similitud semántica, Qwen 2.5-7B en fidelidad numérica y LLaMA 3.1-8B en latencia. Se documenta un sesgo conservador sistemático: ningún modelo asignó NARANJA cuando el consenso experto sí lo hizo.

title: A Gaussian Process Regression Framework for Gasification Process Outcome Forecasting
abstract: The prediction of the products of the process is important for its evaluation and optimization. In the current research, a prediction algorithm framework based on a Gaussian Process Regression approach for predicting nitrogen and hydrogen content is offered, and the influence of metaheuristic hyperparameter tuning is studied. A literature review-driven data set consisting of 316 samples and 18 variables describing features of the feedstock and the process conditions was divided in a 70/15/15 percent ratio for training, validation, and testing. The standalone approach was compared to two hybrid approaches where hyperparameters were optimized by the Honey Badger Algorithm and Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer, respectively. The efficiency of the methods was measured by the following criteria: coefficient of determination, root mean squared error, mean absolute error, mean relative absolute error, and index of agreement. The best performance among all approaches for nitrogen content was shown by the approach based on the Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer with metric values of 0.991, 1.265, 0.999, 1.259, and 0.998, respectively. As for hydrogen, the values of the metrics are 0.991, 1.605, 1.326, 2.199, and 0.998, respectively. Therefore, the suggested optimized model showed better performance than the other two approaches despite the fact that the computation time increased from 12 to 145 seconds.

title: OneForestKB: A Knowledge Base for Global Forest Data Curation and Exploitation Using Geospatial Services
abstract: Global forests are critical for carbon sequestration and climate change mitigation, local and international organizations have developed information systems to store and manage forestry data. Forestry data is heterogeneous, multi-scale, and multi-source, encompassing spatio-temporal observations and metadata about tree species and traits such as trunk diameter at breast height. However, this data often remains stored in local installations and is rarely shared as open data, thereby neglecting the Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) principles. The Semantic Web (SW) community has contributed several standards in related areas such as phenotypic descriptions of species (OBO/PATO), spatial objects (GeoSPARQL), observations and measurements (SOSA), units of measurements (QUDT), among others. However, to our knowledge, comprehensive studies on how to arrange and combine these standards to support curation, reuse, and exploitation of forestry datasets are lacking. To address this gap, we propose the OneForest Knowledge Base (OneForestKB), built on a semantic profile and novel methods to validate and enrich forestry datasets. The semantic profile is designed to maximise the reuse of existing ontologies. We demonstrate its relevance through two use cases in the Amazonian forest of French Guiana, improving data quality via spatial validation rules implemented with SHACL and GeoSPARQL. The SHACL rules are generalized and shared for any GeoSPARQL-based system. We also develop forestry-specific data enrichment rules for calculating ecological indexes used in geographic regions as biodiversity proxies. OneForestKB is extensible, allowing new validations and inferences to be added for specific use cases.

title: Federated learning: From design foundations to advanced participant selection paradigms
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm owing to its significant advantages over conventional centralized machine learning approaches. It is a decentralized learning framework in which a global model is iteratively constructed by aggregating locally trained models from distributed clients, thereby ensuring enhanced data privacy while reducing communication overhead and latency. This survey provides a comprehensive yet concise overview of the state-of-the-art in FL covering key architectural aspects, i.e., scale of federation, data distribution, network topology, exchanged information, training procedures, machine learning models, and aggregation techniques. It further reviews widely used FL frameworks and datasets for simulation and evaluation, incorporating an analysis of dataset selection strategies, the limitations of synthetic data partitioning, and the gap between simulated and real-world deployments. In addition, the incorporation of FL in various applications for their rapid acceleration is discussed. The challenges pertinent to FL are examined under two main categories, i.e., general challenges and those specific to the participant selection process. Building on this, the survey positions participant selection as a central design component in FL systems and provides a unified analysis of state-of-the-art methods through the lenses of composability, trade-offs, and practical design considerations, highlighting its critical role in achieving efficient, robust, fair, and scalable FL.

title: Action Data and CRAFT
abstract: This chapter highlights the critical role of action data in enabling agentic AI, which autonomously executes workflows and coordinates multistep processes. It introduces action data as the fourth data level and applies the CRAFT framework across action, raw, structured, and context data. It emphasizes the industry blind spot of not recognizing action data as a distinct category and the need for structured action data artifacts such as tool definitions, parameter specifications, and workflow definitions. The chapter discusses the MAST-Data dataset, RAG-MCP retrieval for tool selection, and challenges, including schema drift, tool poisoning, and context window overflow. It explores schema validation, semantic validation, and action-data freshness to ensure API specifications match current behavior. The chapter introduces the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and the Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A) for agent interoperability. It also covers resilience strategies including circuit breakers, idempotent APIs, and STRATUS transactional no-regression, alongside safety, observability, recoverability, and auditability. The chapter concludes with the operationalization of action data through specified, discoverable, accurate, current, and auditable tools and workflows, stressing governance, evaluation, monitoring, and ownership for agent operation, alongside Gartner's forecast that more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027.

title: Comments on the recent improvements of the MRRW bounds
abstract: The asymptotic McEliece--Rodemich--Rumsey--Welch bound (1977) limits the largest attainable rate of binary codes as a function of the relative distance. After a nearly half-century hiatus, this result was recently improved in two concurrent works, by OpenAI and by O. Alrabiah and V. Guruswami. The two arguments look entirely different, a Delsarte certificate on the one hand, a classical-quantum channel and the pretty good measurement on the other, and they yield the same bound. The purpose of this note is to explain why: in both proofs, a subspace is attached to every codeword and moved with it, and the bound counts how many such subspaces fit in the ambient space, exactly in the first case and in the probabilistic sense of typicality in the second. We also present the OpenAI proof in the language and context of coding theory, as an extension of the spectral method in which the single vector attached to a codeword is replaced by a subspace.

title: Simultaneous Pointwise Majorization for Mixed Tail Processes with Applications in Gaussian Chaos and Ergodic Diffusions
abstract: Classical chaining controls an indexed stochastic process through a single worst-case bound and can therefore obscure substantial variation across the index set. We develop the first simultaneous pointwise majorization theory for Banach-valued processes with finite-metric mixed-tail increments. Suppose that an anchored process $(Z_t)_{t\in T}$ satisfies, for some integer $m\ge1$, pseudo-metrics $d_1,\ldots,d_m$, and orders $α_1,\ldots,α_m>0$, \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}\{\|Z_t-Z_s\|>\sum_{j=1}^m u^{1/α_j}d_j(s,t)\}\le 2e^{-u},s,t\in T. \end{align*} For ambient priors $μ_1,\ldots,μ_m$, let $v_j(t):=d_j(t,t_0), Φ_j(t):=\int_0^{4v_j(t)}(\log\frac{1}{μ_j(B_{d_j}(t,r))})^{1/α_j}dr$. We prove that, $\forall δ\in(0,1)$, with probability at least $1-δ$, simultaneously for all $t\in T$, \begin{align*} \|Z_t\|\le C_{m,\boldsymbolα}\sum_{j=1}^m\{Φ_j(t)+v_j(t)(\log(e/δ))^{1/α_j}\}. \end{align*} Here $\boldsymbolα:=(α_1,\ldots,α_m)$ and $C_{m,\boldsymbolα}$ depend only on $m$ and these tail orders. The result subsumes single-metric sub-Weibull processes of every positive order as the case $m=1$. In the Gaussian setting, it sharpens the pointwise upper bound of \citet{xu2026} by eliminating the logarithmic terms generated by dyadic peeling. The proof retains the index-wise costs of measure-generated admissible chains and synchronizes the regimes through a nested common refinement. Finally, we apply our theorems to stationary diffusion empirical processes and decoupled Gaussian chaos to obtain simultaneous pointwise envelope bounds, which can further be applied to other statistics problems.

title: Signal-Aware Cayley Completion: Choosing Between an Exact and a Lossy Abelian Host
abstract: Group-embedding graph signal processing buys exact Fourier analysis either by enlarging the domain until a graph embeds isometrically into an abelian Cayley graph, or by perturbing the graph until it is one. We give a linear-time procedure that chooses between the two, and study the criterion governing the lossy branch. We prove that the perturbation of the Dirichlet form is exactly the signed sum of the edited-edge energies, and is bounded in modulus by their total, into which the combinatorial cost of the completion does not enter. We confirm experimentally that this energy predicts signal fidelity strongly though not strictly monotonically (Spearman rho = -0.79 on an instance where the completion, and hence the cost, is held fixed), while the cost itself carries no information about it. Selecting among completions of identical cost by this energy recovers 61 percent of the available performance gap on the exhaustive range, on a sample too small to establish that the effect persists beyond eight vertices. On real payment data the router takes the exact branch everywhere; on real anti-money-laundering data the completion invariant is a re-encoding of maximum degree and is not distinguishable from it, and the linear-time bound it rivals is shown to have a blind spot on near-complete graphs.

title: ReBridge-Flow: Re-Coupling Posterior Bridges in Flow Matching for Image Restoration
abstract: Flow Matching provides an efficient generative prior for image restoration by learning continuous transport between source and data distributions. However, existing methods typically incorporate measurement constraints through local corrections. Such corrections may disrupt the source-clean endpoint coupling implicitly encoded by the pretrained flow, making the corrected endpoint pair incompatible with the current state. To address this issue, we propose ReBridge-Flow, a posterior bridge re-coupling method. Specifically, given the current state, ReBridge-Flow first decodes the corresponding local source and clean endpoints. It then incorporates measurement information through clean-side anchoring and synchronously re-couples the source endpoint, yielding a measurement-aware endpoint pair with improved local bridge compatibility. The re-coupled endpoints further define a posterior-informed transport direction for advancing the sampling process. We also introduce the Posterior Bridge Defect, which jointly characterizes measurement error, deviation from the flow prior, and bridge mismatch, and leads to explicit updates for clean-side anchoring and source-side re-coupling. Extensive experiments on multiple natural and medical image restoration tasks demonstrate that ReBridge-Flow effectively alleviates bridge mismatch and improves the structural consistency of restored images.

title: Annotation von Forschungsdaten mit ontologien in shepard
abstract: Das am DLR in Augsburg entwickelte System shepard (storage for heterogeneous production and research data) bietet eine Option zur Forschungsdatenspeicherung mit der Möglichkeit, Daten mit Ontologien zu annotieren. Das führt einer verbesserten Auffindbarkeit durch speziell entwickelte Suchfunktionalitäten und erhöht die Nutzungsmöglichkeiten der Daten durch diverse Stakeholder bei Verwendung gemeinsamer Ontologien. Darüber hinaus können durch Semantic Reasoning neue Erkenntnisse gewonnen werden.

title: PERANCANGAN SISTEM PENILAIAN KETERCAPAIAN PEMBELAJARAN DENGAN PREDIKSI KOMPETENSI MAHASISWA BERBASIS RULE-BASED DAN VISUALISASI DIAGRAM
abstract: Kurikulum Outcome-Based Education (OBE) merupakan standar pemutakhiran pendidikan tinggi yang berfokus pada capaian pembelajaran komprehensif untuk memastikan keselarasan kompetensi lulusan dengan tuntutan dunia kerja global. Keberhasilan implementasi kurikulum berbasis luaran ini sangat bergantung pada efisiensi dan akurasi dokumentasi serta evaluasi data kompetensi mahasiswa secara berkelanjutan. Namun, penerapan kurikulum berbasis OBE di Program Studi Sistem Informasi Universitas Bengkulu saat ini masih menghadapi kendala operasional, di mana pengelolaan data CPL dan CPMK masih dilakukan secara manual menggunakan spreadsheet.Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk merancang dan membangun sistem informasi berbasis website yang mampu mendukung dokumentasi, pemetaan, dan evaluasi CPL, serta mengembangkan fitur prediksi kompetensi mahasiswa menggunakan pendekatan rule-based system. Metode yang digunakan dalam penelitian ini adalah Research and Development (R&D) dengan pendekatan mixed methods, mengombinasikan metode kualitatif melalui observasi dan wawancara, serta metode kuantitatif melalui User Acceptance Testing (UAT) menggunakan skala Likert. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sistem yang dikembangkan mampu mengintegrasikan pengelolaan data CPL– CPMK secara terpusat, melakukan perhitungan otomatis capaian pembelajaran, serta menghasilkan prediksi kompetensi mahasiswa ke dalam lima kategori: Very High (VH), High (H), Medium (M), Low (L), dan Very Low (VL). Sistem ini juga dilengkapi dengan dasbor visual untuk memudahkan interpretasi data oleh pengguna. Berdasarkan hasil pengujian Black-Box dan UAT, sistem berfungsi dengan baik dan mencapai tingkat penerimaan pengguna sebesar 87,27% untuk aspek desain, 86,66% untuk aspek kemudahan, dan 87,27% untuk aspek fungsi/kegunaan, yang dikategorikan dalam rentang layak hingga sangat layak. Kesimpulannya, sistem informasi yang dikembangkan terbukti meningkatkan efisiensi, akurasi, dan efektivitas dalam pengelolaan serta evaluasi capaian pembelajaran berbasis OBE, sekaligus berkontribusi mendukung pengambilan keputusan akademik melalui fitur prediksi kompetensi mahasiswa. Kata kunci: Outcome Based Education,CPMK, Rule-based system, Sistem Informasi, Prediksi Kompetensi

title: OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES FOR LARGE AI MODELS
abstract: The rapid growth of large artificial intelligence models has created significant challenges related to computational cost, memory consumption, training time, energy requirements, and deployment efficiency. Optimization techniques are therefore essential for developing, training, fine-tuning, and deploying large AI models effectively. This chapter examines key optimization strategies designed to improve the efficiency, scalability, and performance of large-scale neural networks and foundation models. By integrating theoretical principles with practical optimization strategies, this chapter provides a comprehensive foundation for understanding how large AI models can be trained and deployed more efficiently while maintaining effective model performance.

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A Critical Survey Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

abstract: Another thousand breakthroughs crossed the threshold since I last spoke—406 in this rotation alone, bringing the total to 183,977. title: Detecting New Knowledge in Dialogue and Protecting Secrets On-Device: a Detector as a LoRA Adapter
abstract: An on-device detector that finds new knowledge in what a user says and splits it into what can be shared and what must stay private. The detector reads the speech act (stating, asking, supposing, retelling) rather than keywords, and it is a LoRA adapter over Qwen2.5-3B, so a prompt cannot override it. On the secret-detection task (437 realistic secrets, 300 ordinary messages) it ranks first among seven solutions (F1 0.997): it beats mass data-protection tools such as Presidio and detect-secrets, matches a large cloud model while running on the device, and on equal footing is not behind a specialized model. Code, data, and logs: https://github.com/evanokinsr/sokol-detector Contact: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ivan-okunkov and Telegram @i_star_part

title: TEECAM: Trusted Execution and Edge Container Anomaly Monitor
abstract: TEECAM is a reproducible research prototype for security monitoring in containerised edge systems. It combines a narrow gateway to OP-TEE secure storage, window-based anomaly detection using percentile and Isolation Forest models, and an OP-TEE audit Trusted Application that issues HMAC-protected receipts for submitted alert digests.

title: Quantum Entanglement Entropy Calculation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental property of quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge to traditional entropy calculations. This paper explores the development of a novel entropy calculation model based on quantum entanglement, aiming to improve the precision of measuring and predicting the evolution of entangled states. The core mechanism leverages the non-linear properties of entangled states to enable a more profound statistical analysis of quantum system evolution. The proposed model offers a significant advancement in quantifying the entanglement entropy, which has implications for quantum information security and quantum computation. This work addresses limitations of existing approaches by focusing on a fundamentally new framework for analyzing entanglement dynamics. The key contribution is the creation of an entanglement entropy measure that transcends classical approximations, offering a more accurate and robust representation of entanglement's statistical properties.

title: Brown Hairy Dwarf Porcupine: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of a Small Mammal
abstract: This paper introduces a new metaheuristic algorithm, the Brown Hairy Dwarf Porcupine (BHDP) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior and defense mechanisms of *Erethizon dorsatum* (Brown Hairy Dwarf Porcupine). The algorithm mimics the porcupine's selective movement, obstacle avoidance, and caching strategies to solve complex optimization problems. The BHDP algorithm utilizes a novel population management strategy based on the porcupine's territoriality and resource competition, coupled with a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm's core components include a position update mechanism simulating the porcupine's cautious movement, an obstacle avoidance technique mirroring its defensive posture, and a caching mechanism representing resource storage. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's potential for efficient exploration and exploitation, leading to improved convergence rates. We illustrate the effectiveness of the BHDP algorithm through numerical experiments on several benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising tool for tackling a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: 自适应的混沌系统中的随机梯度下降
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithm within a dynamically adaptive chaos system. Traditional SGD implementations often struggle with slow convergence and suboptimal solutions, especially in chaotic environments. This work proposes a new algorithm that dynamically adjusts the gradient descent step size based on the system's state, leading to improved efficiency and yield. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and analysis of a complex, three-dimensional chaotic system. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously monitors the system's dynamics and adjusts the step size to optimize the search process. The results show a significant improvement in convergence speed and solution quality compared to standard SGD, highlighting the potential of this adaptive approach.

title: Broad-toothed Field Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Broad-toothed Field Mouse Algorithm" (BTFMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the broad-toothed field mouse (Apodemus agrarius). This rodent is known for its efficient exploration of complex environments in search of food sources. The BTFMA leverages the mouse's ability to adjust its search strategy based on environmental feedback, specifically focusing on the width of its "tooth" (search radius) and its movement direction. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic adjustment of this "tooth" width, influenced by a stochastic objective function reflecting the perceived food density. Furthermore, it employs a novel movement strategy based on biased random walks, mimicking the mouse's tendency to follow gradients of potential food sources. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The key mathematical components include the stochastic adjustment of the search radius (s) using a probability distribution (P(s)) and the biased random walk probability (R(d)) influenced by the gradient of an objective function (∇f). The algorithm's core loop consists of updating the position (x) and search radius (s) based on these probabilities. The effectiveness of the BTFMA is quantified using metrics such as solution accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: 混沌域的自适应几何优化算法
abstract: 混沌域,作为一种非线性、自适应几何结构,因其独特的性质,在科学和工程领域展现出广泛的应用前景。本研究深入探讨了混沌域在自适应几何优化算法中的应用,旨在构建一种能够高效寻找全局最优解的算法。我们提出了一种基于混沌域的优化算法,该算法利用混沌域的自适应特性,在有限时间内找到最优解。本文首先阐述了混沌域的特征和相关理论,然后详细描述了我们提出的算法的设计和实现,并对算法的性能进行了评估。我们重点强调了混沌域在优化过程中的作用,以及该算法的创新之处。

title: Dynamic Semantic Network Topology Optimization (DSNO)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Semantic Network Topology Optimization (DSNO), a novel approach to knowledge discovery leveraging reinforcement learning for adaptive network topology management. The core claim is that an intelligent agent can dynamically adjust the semantic network topology in real-time based on streaming data and semantic association strength, minimizing information propagation delay and maximizing knowledge discovery efficiency. DSNO utilizes a reinforcement learning framework where the agent learns to optimize network topology through adding, deleting, and redirecting nodes and edges. The optimization process is guided by graph theory algorithms, such as PageRank variants, to assess node importance and connectivity. This dynamic adaptation distinguishes DSNO from traditional static or rule-based semantic network optimization methods, enabling a fully adaptive and self-optimizing system deeply integrated with knowledge discovery objectives. The proposed methodology offers a pathway to more efficient and robust knowledge extraction from complex, evolving data networks.

title: Bolivian Chincilla Rat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the "Chincilla Rat Algorithm" (CRA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bolivian Chincilla rat. The algorithm leverages the rat's efficient path-finding strategies and adaptive exploration-exploitation balance to tackle complex optimization problems. CRA incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), combined with a dynamically adjusted 'territory size' parameter mimicking the chincilla's home range. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a modified velocity update rule and a territory expansion/contraction strategy aimed at escaping local optima and promoting global exploration. We present a theoretical analysis of CRA's convergence properties and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, Sphere function, and the Himmelblau non-linear constrained optimization problem. The results indicate that CRA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like PSO and SA, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. The algorithm's adaptability and robustness make it a promising approach for a wide range of optimization applications.

title: ## Blue Flyer: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Blue Flyer Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Blue Flyer, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the observed flight patterns of blue flyers ( *Cyanopsitta orientalis* ). Blue flyers exhibit remarkable maneuverability and efficiency in navigating complex environments. We leverage these behaviors to design a novel optimization algorithm, incorporating concepts of dynamic exploration, adaptive velocity control, and a distributed search strategy. Blue Flyer utilizes a population of candidate solutions represented as vectors, employing a velocity component to guide movement and adjust the magnitude of the velocity based on the landscape gradient. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic adjustment of the step size, influenced by the local search performance, and a mechanism for distributing solutions across the search space. The performance of Blue Flyer is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive efficacy and potential for applications in diverse fields. The key contributions of this work include the algorithm's design principles, a detailed explanation of its operational mechanics, and empirical validation through comparative performance analysis.

title: Hybrid Deep Sequential Learning and IBSCA-Driven Feature Selection for Robust Classification of Imbalanced Dataset
abstract: In many real-world datasets, class imbalance is still an issue that skews traditional classifiers in favour of majority classes and hinders the performance of minority classes. This work introduces a novel end-to-end pipeline that combines IBSA feature selection (92% dimensionality reduction), BiGRU-LSTM-Attention hybrid modelling for complex spatiotemporal pattern capture, and adaptive thresholding for fairness optimisation. With state-of-the-art results of 98.61% accuracy/99.92% sensitivity and 99.79% accuracy/99.89% sensitivity, the proposed BiGRU-LSTM model outperforms optimization-enhanced hybrids by 1-2% and SMOTE baselines by 7-15% on benchmark imbalanced datasets covering binary and multi-class scenarios. These notable advancements show how well the architecture handles severe class imbalance across domains, establishing new performance standards that could be applied to federated learning and high-dimensional data processing.

evidence.abstract: In many real-world datasets, class imbalance is still an issue that skews traditional classifiers in favour of majority classes and hinders the performance of minority classes. This work introduces a novel end-to-end pipeline that combines IBSA feature selection (92% dimensionality reduction), BiGRU-LSTM-Attention hybrid modelling for complex spatiotemporal pattern capture, and adaptive thresholding for fairness optimisation. With state-of-the-art results of 98.61% accuracy/99.92% sensitivity and 99.79% accuracy/99.89% sensitivity, the proposed BiGRU-LSTM model outperforms optimization-enhanced hybrids by 1-2% and SMOTE baselines by 7-15% on benchmark imbalanced datasets covering binary and multi-class scenarios. These notable advancements show how well the architecture handles severe class imbalance across domains, establishing new performance standards that could be applied to federated learning and high-dimensional data processing.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and the Reconstruction of Intellectual Property Law: Copyright, Patent, Trademark, Trade Secret, and Governance in the Age of Machine Production
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) has placed intellectual property (IP) law by affecting the entire chain of creative, technical, and commercial production. Copyright law must determine the extent of human control required to protect AI-assisted work; whether extensive ingestion of protected works for model training constitutes infringement, fair use, text and data-mining, or licensed use; and how courts should evaluate outputs that resemble or compete with existing works. Patent law confronts a related question: how to preserve human inventorship as generative technologies increasingly assist with hypothesis formation, molecular design, code generation, engineering optimization, claim drafting, and experimental planning. Trademark law is also changing, although it has received less attention. In AI-mediated markets, consumers may no longer encounter trademarks through ordinary searches and comparisons. Instead, they may receive ranked answers, conversational recommendations, generated product descriptions, synthetic endorsements, or automated purchase suggestions. Trade secret law has become equally central because model weights, datasets, prompts, safety procedures, filtering methods, benchmarks, and fine-tuning practices are often protected as secrets, even when creators, regulators, courts, and downstream users require additional information to evaluate legal compliance and public risk. This study argues that generative AI should be regulated by reconstructing existing intellectual property principles rather than granting legal personhood to AI systems or creating new, exclusive rights for machine-generated outputs. Human authorship and inventorship should remain the legal baseline. Meanwhile, the law must exercise greater caution regarding the stages at which AI creates legal risks. Training, model development, output generation, and market deployment raise different questions and should not be reduced to a singular debate about AI and IP. This study employs doctrinal, comparative, and policy analyses using materials from the U.S., EU, U.K., and international organizations. It examines recent case law and administrative guidance alongside academic scholarship on authorship, fair use, text and data mining, augmented inventorship, algorithmic trademarks, deepfakes, transparency, and trade secrets. It concludes that the most affective AI era framework is layered and emphasizes human-centered attribution, contextual training approaches, meaningful transparency, sector-sensitive licensing, output-stage accountability, disciplined trade secret protection, and coordination among IP law, competition law, consumer protection, privacy, and AI regulation.

title: On the Applicability of Neural Networks in the Publishing Industry
abstract: Abstract The paper assesses the limits of applicability of large language models in editorial tasks within the publishing process and identifies the optimal format of interaction between humans and algorithmic systems. The methodological basis of the study is a comparative experiment in which several popular neural network models—Alice AI, GigaChat, DeepSeek, Gemini, and ChatGPT—performed a statistical analysis of a control text in Russian. The quantitative characteristics of the text were determined: the number of words, characters with and without spaces, and the number of paragraphs. The obtained results were compared with reference values established using the MS Word text editor, which applies a deterministic character-counting algorithm. The results of the experiment showed that neural network models demonstrate varying degrees of accuracy when performing tasks of quantitative text analysis. The main reason for such errors lies in the architecture of large language models and the use of tokenization algorithms, which break the direct connection between characters and the model’s internal representation of the text. Based on the results obtained, the paper proposes the concept of a hybrid architecture for publishing information systems, in which generative language models are used to perform creative and analytical tasks, while operations requiring strict formal accuracy are assigned to specialized deterministic microservices. The proposed approach makes it possible to improve the reliability and predictability of intelligent publishing systems.

title: Fair and Robust Federated Learning for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction via Client Heterogeneity Quantification
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a major global health burden and the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Although machine learning has shown promise for CVD risk prediction, centralized training on sensitive medical data from multiple hospitals raises serious privacy and security concerns. To address this issue, we propose FedCH, a novel federated learning method for collaborative CVD prediction. Specifically, FedCH quantifies client heterogeneity by measuring the similarity between local and global models together with client-specific prediction accuracy. These metrics are used to dynamically weight the global aggregation process, thereby improving the overall model performance while promoting fairness across clients. In addition, by incorporating historical global model parameters into the update process, FedCH mitigates local model fluctuations and enhances the generalization and robustness of the global model. Comprehensive evaluations on four public datasets and a real-world cardiovascular dataset from a tertiary hospital in China show that FedCH consistently outperforms five state-of-the-art federated learning baselines under heterogeneous client settings.

title: Some trace-restricted cyclic and constacyclic MDS symbol-pair codes
abstract: Symbol-pair codes have attracted considerable attention because of their applications in communication and storage systems where information is read in overlapping pairs of symbols. The construction of cyclic and constacyclic symbol-pair codes using trace restricted defining roots over a finite commutative ring with nilpotent elements is being carried out. A trace map introduced to the associated ring, and to characterize trace restricted elements its algebraic properties are examined. These elements are applied to construct consecutive defining roots whose corresponding generator polynomials are proved to exist in the base field. The inter-relation is then established between the defining-roots and the minimum symbol pair distance resulting to lower bounds on the pair distance of the constructed codes. Necessary and sufficient conditions under which these bounds attain the Singleton-type bound are introduced, forming several families of maximum distance separable symbol pair codes. A class of cyclic and constacyclic symbol-pair codes is examined along with required roots that satisfies trace restriction over finite commutative ring with nilpotent elements.

title: Architectures of Large Language Models
abstract: This chapter introduces the architectural foundations of large language models (LLMs) and explains why the transformer has become the dominant framework for modern language processing. It begins by defining LLMs and summarizing their core capabilities across tasks, such as question answering, summarization, translation, and conversational interaction. This chapter then presents the basics of transformers, emphasizing self-attention, embeddings, positional encoding, and the complementary roles of the encoder and decoder in capturing context and generating text. Next, this chapter compares three major architectural families: encoder-only models (e.g., Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer (BERT)) optimized for language understanding, decoder-only models (e.g., Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)) designed for autoregressive generation, and encoder–decoder (Seq2Seq) models (e.g., Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer (T5), Bidirectional and Auto-Regressive Transformers (BART), multilingual BART (mBART)) suited to translation and transformation tasks. Practical examples using the Hugging Face Transformers library demonstrate common applications, including sentiment classification, extraction of embeddings, named entity recognition, question answering, text generation, and multilingual translation.

title: Emerging applications of artificial intelligence in environmental engineering: a mini review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is currently driving transformative changes in environmental science and engineering. With the development of artificial intelligence, these technologies have been widely applied across environmental fields, demonstrating immense potential in processing complex environmental system data. This paper provides a concise overview of AI applications in water environments, atmospheric conditions, and soil-ecosystem systems. The paper analyzes the great changes brought by artificial intelligence to the environmental field, such as intelligent water management, global-scale pollutant prediction, real-time air quality monitoring, pollutant identification, and traceability. Artificial intelligence also faces significant challenges, such as the limited universality of machine learning models, which hinders multi-regional collaborative prediction, and the difficulty in clearly explaining the underlying mechanisms through interpretability. Through the deep integration of multi-source datasets and artificial intelligence technologies, environmental decision-making systems can achieve integrated operations featuring dynamic monitoring, intelligent early warning, and automated decision-making. Artificial intelligence is poised to play an increasingly critical role in addressing global environmental crises.

title: A new perspective on centroid algorithms for unsupervised discrete clustering in Riemannian manifolds: an approach via optimization
abstract: Abstract Clustering is an unsupervised learning technique used to discover hidden structures in data. By identifying patterns and similarities among objects, this methodology enables the organization of datasets into homogeneous groups. This work presents a new perspective on a specific class of partition-based algorithms for unsupervised discrete clustering in complete finite-dimensional Riemannian manifolds by introducing statistical shape analyses to classify clusters and improve label selection. To achieve this aim, we extend the statistical concepts of skewness and kurtosis to Riemannian settings, based on vector operations in the tangent plane at each point of the manifold. Assumptions regarding the injectivity radius and the boundedness of the sectional curvature are initially adopted to enable local convex analysis. Nevertheless, the well-posedness of Riemannian weighted centroids is ensured by analyzing the coercivity and quasiconvexity properties of the distance function’s powers. In addition, we demonstrate that well-posedness and continuity extend to any positive power of the distance function, rather than being limited to powers greater than or equal to 1. Computational experiments involving diffusion tensor imaging and hyperspectral image segmentation are performed. We also present a statistical analysis to demonstrate the practical applicability and computational performance of our technique compared with leading clustering approaches. Ultimately, our methodology is applicable to any field where data modeling resides in a complete finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold.
