title: Mapping Your Data for AI
abstract: This chapter delineates the core concepts of AI systems, categorizing them into perception AI, which extracts structure from raw signals; analytical AI, which identifies patterns in organized facts; generative AI, which synthesizes content from learned knowledge; and agentic AI, which executes actions through tools and workflows. It emphasizes the importance of data quality, distinguishing between raw data (complete capture, accuracy, timeliness, and provenance) and structured data (clean tables, consistent schemas, resolved entities, and documented relationships). The chapter also highlights the role of vector embeddings, knowledge graphs, and semantic layers in organizing context data, and the use of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ground model responses with external information. Key challenges include hallucination rates in legal research tools (17-33%) and cancer-information chatbots, as well as data cascades and missing dependencies in AI projects. The chapter underscores the necessity of dependency-aware planning, governance maturity, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for tool and context exposure, with a focus on reducing hallucinations and improving retrieval quality, coverage, provenance, and freshness. It also discusses the adoption of generative AI and its value generation in early 2024, emphasizing the critical role of data dependencies and the CRAFT priorities (complete, retrievable, accurate, fresh, traceable) in ensuring AI readiness.

title: OR-Transformer: Scaling Real-Time Decision-Making to 1,000 Items
abstract: Modern supply chain operations can require coordinating replenishment across thousands of heterogeneous items under correlated stochastic demand, heterogeneous lead times, and shared fixed ordering costs, yielding observation spaces exceeding $10^4$ dimensions. At this scale, rolling-horizon stochastic mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) become prohibitively slow, while standard reinforcement learning (RL) methods face increasingly challenging credit assignment in high-dimensional action spaces. We introduce OR-Transformer, a deep reinforcement learning framework for joint replenishment under stochastic demand, with an item-permutation-equivariant Transformer architecture and pathwise-gradient training through the inventory dynamics. Across problem sizes up to 1,024 inventory items, OR-Transformer increasingly outperforms learning-based and rolling-horizon MILP baselines as scale grows. It also reduces online decision-making time by over 4 million times relative to MILP solvers, enabling real-time, large-scale deep RL in supply chain operations.

title: Support of Dyson Brownian Motion
abstract: We consider beta-Dyson Brownian motion, with β>= 1, started from a deterministic configuration with uniformly bounded support. Let μ_t be the semicircular free-convolution flow issued from the initial empirical measure, and set S_t = supp(μ_t). For every fixed T, ε> 0, with probability at least 1 - C exp(-(log n)^2), every particle remains within an epsilon-neighborhood of S_t for all 0 <= t <= T. The result holds from time zero, requires no regularity assumption at the initial spectral edges, and applies to multi-cut supports with macroscopic interior gaps. A key ingredient is a deterministic local resolvent exclusion principle: an o((n η)^(-1)) comparison of Stieltjes transforms on a complex disc above a real point separated from the reference support excludes eigenvalues from the corresponding real interval. This gives a model-independent mechanism for converting local resolvent estimates into spectral confinement.

title: A Composable Evaluation System for Reproducible Omni-Modal Foundation Model Evaluation
abstract: Building an omni-modal foundation model means evaluating it across text, image, video, and audio. Excellent evaluation toolkits exist for each modality, but their inference engines, prompt conventions, and metric implementations are mutually incompatible, so practitioners end up maintaining separate environments for every toolchain and still struggle to compare results across them. OmniEvaluator grew out of this need in our own model development: rather than reimplementing benchmarks, it connects existing inference engines and curated evaluation libraries at a higher level, exposing four inference backends, four evaluation frameworks, and over a thousand benchmarks through a single interface. Every run is recorded as an artifact capturing the full configuration for exact reproduction, and results flow into a shared dashboard for cross-model comparison. A federated mode shares GPU inference servers across concurrent evaluations, and a built-in verifier, small enough to run on CPU, keeps its score stable across engines and prompts where rule-based scoring fluctuates under configuration mismatch, matching cost-efficient commercial LLM judges without their recurring API cost. The system, demo video, and dashboard are publicly available. (https://github.com/naver-ai/omni-evaluator)

title: Optical free space extreme learning machine for the implementation of emergent complex systems
abstract: Cellular automata conform a set of computational models which evolve with a reduced set of simple rules, yet still are able to show extremely complex emergent phenomena such as fractals and universal computation. Despite their apparent simplicity, they have shown great potential in simulating natural systems and solving challenging computational tasks such as classification and image generation. Instead of implementing cellular automata purely at the software level, it is desirable to design novel analog computing platforms that physically evolve following the automata's underlying rules, thereby reducing power requirements and latency. Here, we introduce an optical extreme learning machine for the simulation of a wide range of cellular automata. Our system operates in free space, and uses a spatial light modulator to encode the evolution rules of the system, while coherent wave propagation performs the corresponding computations. Our results demonstrate a simple, fully-programmable, cost and power efficient, and easy to build and align platform for the implementation of a wide range of complex computational systems such as elementary cellular automata, Conway's Game of Life, and two-dimensional Turing machines.

title: Test-Time Adaptation with Steering Primitives for Realigning Representations
abstract: This work investigates test-time adaptation, the problem of adapting a pretrained model to distribution shift at deployment using only unlabeled test data. Existing methods typically adapt by updating the model’s own parameters, which limits both what can be adapted and where adaptation can occur within the network, and leaves the pretrained solution vulnerable to error accumulation and forgetting. This work instead keeps the pretrained backbone entirely frozen and steers its intermediate rep resentations through lightweight learnable modules inserted at stage boundaries and optimized directly from the test stream, requiring neither source data nor supervised warm-up. Each module is trained with a gated objective that reduces prediction un certainty only when adaptation is beneficial, a diversity regularizer that prevents class collapse, and a multi-depth anchor that stabilizes adaptation and limits drift. The analysis shows that steering early representations is the most effective strategy, and that the same module transfers across convolutional and Vision Transformer architec tures. evidence.title: Test-Time Adaptation with Steering Primitives for Realigning Representations
evidence.abstract: This work investigates test-time adaptation, the problem of adapting a pretrained model to distribution shift at deployment using only unlabeled test data. Existing methods typically adapt by updating the model’s own parameters, which limits both what can be adapted and where adaptation can occur within the network, and leaves the pretrained solution vulnerable to error accumulation and forgetting. This work instead keeps the pretrained backbone entirely frozen and steers its intermediate rep resentations through lightweight learnable modules inserted at stage boundaries and optimized directly from the test stream, requiring neither source data nor supervised warm-up. Each module is trained with a gated objective that reduces prediction un certainty only when adaptation is beneficial, a diversity regularizer that prevents class collapse, and a multi-depth anchor that stabilizes adaptation and limits drift. The analysis shows that steering early representations is the most effective strategy, and that the same module transfers across convolutional and Vision Transformer architec tures. Across standard corruption benchmarks and diverse normalization schemes, the proposed method matches or outperforms approaches that adapt orders of magnitude more parameters, remains robust across a wide range of batch sizes, and preserves source-domain performance during continual adaptation.

title: Beyond DCR:HSS and PCFs from Subgroup Indistinguishability
abstract: We construct homomorphic secret sharing (HSS) and pseudorandom correlation functions (PCFs) in a general group-theoretic framework, with security based on the subgroup indistinguishability (SgI) assumption introduced by Brakerski and Goldwasser (Crypto 2010). Under certain instantiations of this framework, SgI corresponds to decisional composite residuosity (DCR), but other instantiations are possible as well. Hence, our work expands the set of assumptions that imply HSS and PCFs. Our constructions crucially rely on the existence of an efficient distributed discrete logarithm (DDLog) algorithm for the utilized group. We construct a new DDLog algorithm that works in general groups as long as the order t of the base is smooth. In particular, our DDLog supports the prime-power case, which was previously an open problem. Moreover, we apply a divide-and conquer optimization that significantly improves the performance from O(log2 t/loglogt) group operations (Abram et al., Crypto 2022) to O(logtloglogt). Toward constructing PCFs, we introduce a new notion of public-coin subgroup indistinguishability (PC-SgI). We show that, in certain instantiations, SgI implies PC-SgI, so no new assumption is required. We then obtain PCFs for VOLE, OT, OLE, and degree-two correlations, all generically under PC-SgI. Our PCFs for OLE and degree-two correlations additionally relyon the sparse LPN assumption. Along the way, we discover and patch two security issues in prior work: first, an attack on decisional Diffie–Hellman (DDH) in the Joye–Libert instantiation by Abram et al. (Crypto 2022), and second, a flaw in the security proofs of optimized variants of the IKNP OT extension protocol and of many silent OT extension protocols.

title: PROMPT INJECTION AND JAILBREAK ATTACKS ON LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: THREATS AND DEFENSE STRATEGIES
abstract: The evolution of large language models has paved the way towards more advanced artificial intelligence solutions and allowed breakthrough advancements in various areas including natural language processing, content creation, software development, education, healthcare, cybersecurity and many others. Nonetheless, as LLMs are incorporated into the real-life applications, they face increasing security challenges such as prompt injection and jailbreak attacks. This chapter aims to provide the comprehensive summary of the emerging security threats for LLMs by giving the definitions of the core concepts related to the transformer-based architecture of the LLMs, prompt engineering and overall LLMs ecosystem. Further, the paper will describe the taxonomy of prompt injection attacks including direct injection, indirect injection, context manipulation and data exfiltration and jailbreak attacks which are defined as role-playing attacks, multi-turn jailbreaks, obfuscation and automatic adversarial prompt generation. The paper will also discuss current defence mechanisms including prompt filtering, alignment, AI guardrails and safe agent framework and will highlight their benefits and drawbacks in relation to the constantly evolving attacks. Finally, the open problems that remain unsolved in the area will be mentioned, namely agentic AI, adaptive attacks and benchmarking.

title: White-Box Complete Neural Networks without Performance Trade-offs: Principle and Realization
abstract: Abstract We demonstrate that the black-box nature of standard neural networks stems from two independent defects of the activation function: sharing and non-polynomiality. The former induces neuronal entanglement; the latter obstructs exact semantics. Based on this principle, we show a minimal modification—returning nonlinearity freedom to each neuron at order two—which removes both defects at once, achieving white-box completeness (WBC): the conversion between a universal-approximation neural network and a computationally universal rule set becomes exact and well-conditioned. The modification preserves full computational properties and matches the performance of first-tier conventional activations across six vision and language benchmarks. On visual tasks devoid of pre-assigned semantic features, we exemplify, for the first time, three ultimate abilities of trustworthy artificial intelligence: extraction of the global, sample-irrelevant decision function with errors merely at cumulative floating-point level, training-free precise model manipulation, human knowledge injection. Beyond transparency, we use zero-forgetting incremental learning to demonstrate the potential impact of highly controllable models on other domains. Our work proves that the black-box character of neural networks is not an inevitable destiny but two correctable design flaws. Keywords: White-box completeness; Black-box problem; Explainable artificial intelligence; Neural network editing; Incremental learning; Trustworthy artificial intelligence.

title: Adaptive Neuron Models: A Filtering Mechanism for Enhanced Efficiency and Generalization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a filtering mechanism within adaptive neuron models to improve computational efficiency and generalization performance. The core claim is that introducing this mechanism can significantly reduce the computational complexity of these models, leading to faster training and enhanced generalization capabilities. The proposed mechanism leverages an attention-based system that dynamically adjusts information pathways within the neuron model based on neuron activation states and input signal weights. This approach mitigates redundant information transfer, resulting in a more streamlined and efficient model. The resulting model demonstrates improved performance compared to standard adaptive neuron models, particularly in scenarios with high-dimensional input or complex relationships. This work provides a novel approach to optimizing adaptive neuron models for a wider range of applications.

title: Quantum Random Number Generator-Based Cryptographic Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores the design of cryptographic algorithms leveraging the inherent randomness of quantum random number generators (QRNGs). Traditional cryptographic algorithms often rely on pseudo-random number generators (PRNGs), which are deterministic and therefore vulnerable to attacks if their internal state is compromised. QRNGs, on the other hand, derive their randomness from quantum mechanical phenomena, offering a fundamentally unpredictable source of numbers. This research investigates the application of QRNGs to enhance cryptographic security, focusing on constructing algorithms that exploit this unique property. The core claim is that utilizing QRNG characteristics allows for the design of more secure cryptographic algorithms. The proposed mechanism involves capitalizing on the non-deterministic nature of QRNGs to build algorithms with heightened security levels. This approach presents a novel security guarantee method by incorporating true randomness into cryptographic processes. We examine specific algorithm designs and analyze their security implications compared to traditional PRNG-based approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion on the challenges and future directions of utilizing QRNGs in cryptography.
